aspects.what_would_make_it_8: No hard-coded counts anywhere, reference docs regenerated or dated within weeks, and a short, current entry point.

overall_notes: The engineering scaffolding is strong: strict TypeScript in src, about 3,900 tests, many build gates, a price-default suppressor, the rollover hold, hard-stop concerns, and axe-clean markup. Several of these visibly stopped bad data (the New York ONX exhibition, 2027 rollover rows, venue-default prices). The product surface still falls short in three areas. (1) Wrong facts still get through: the athinorama tour-range conflation publishes about 60 indexable pages placing Perses and Medea at Lycabettus 'running' through late September, when the source lists one night at Theatro Vrachon, and a rock gig is typed as theatre on the homepage. (2) The Greek-primary site has no Greek descriptions, English UI strings leak into Greek pages and Greek ones into English pages, and 35% of upcoming events have only a templated one-liner. (3) Operations and measurement: 4 of the last 8 daily deploys were refused over a dirty source tree, so the live 'Απόψε' showed yesterday's events, and the citation and crawler measurement the project exists for is still null or empty. Counts on public surfaces (3,800 pages, 809 'live', 2,423 tests) are hard-coded or stale. Scores were given against the local build unless noted; live-only observations are labelled.
